My Career Plan

A career goal gives your college choices direction. Exploring the work you hope to do can help you choose a program that fits, understand why your courses matter, and adjust your plan as you learn more. You do not need to have everything settled today.

Starting Out · Discover your interests

Identify the kinds of activities and work environments that appeal to you. Record a possible direction, then talk it through with a Career Center manager.

Career Interest Assessment ↗

Making Progress · Research the work

Compare occupations, education routes, workplace settings, and the skills employers expect. Revisit your goal as your experience grows.

Job Matchup ↗My Next Move ↗

Workplace Skills · Practice before graduation

Knowing about a skill is a start. Practice it in a class, campus job, internship, or community activity so you have a real example to share with an employer.

Explore the eight NACE career readiness competencies ↗. The Equity + Inclusion competency is currently under review by NACE; check its site for the latest guidance.

Career + Self-Development

Keep learning, seek feedback, and make purposeful choices about your next steps.

Try it: Ask a supervisor or instructor for feedback and act on one suggestion.

Communication

Share ideas clearly and listen to understand what others need.

Try it: Explain a project update to someone outside your class or team.

Critical Thinking

Examine information, weigh options, and explain how you reached a decision.

Try it: Compare two possible solutions to a class or workplace problem.

Equity + Inclusion

Work respectfully with people whose perspectives and experiences differ from yours.

Try it: Invite different viewpoints before a group makes a decision.

Leadership

Help a group move toward a shared goal, whether or not you hold a title.

Try it: Organize a project milestone and support a teammate who needs help.

Professionalism

Be dependable, prepared, and accountable for your work.

Try it: Confirm expectations early and deliver an assignment or shift task on time.

Teamwork

Share responsibility and work through differences to complete something together.

Try it: Agree on roles for a team project and follow through on your part.

Technology

Choose and use tools thoughtfully to get work done.

Try it: Learn a relevant tool and explain how it improved your process.

My plan at Collin
